subject: Structuring seat-linked observability credits and retention tiers
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Roberts <elena@acmedata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Structuring seat-linked observability credits and retention tiers

Elena — thanks again for the time today. Attached is a first-pass proposal that separates the observability offering into: 1) base telemetry (included in hosting), 2) advanced tracing & retention (add-on), and 3) dashboard seats (optional).

Key ask from your side was a way to anchor observability credits to user seats so quarter-over-quarter usage spikes (product launches) don't blow the unit economics. The attached PDF includes a model that converts "seat commitments" into monthly retention credits and a fallback overage rate.

Quick summary here: 
- Proposed commitment: 250 dashboard seats / 12 months
- Included retention credits: 6 TB month-equivalent (applied as prefix retention + trace storage)
- Tracing: 14-day default, with optional 30/90-day tiers at incremental per-GB rates
- Seat-linked credits: for every additional 50 committed seats, +2 TB retention credit/mo (stackable)
- Overage: $0.23/GB for retention beyond credits; we can convert to a blended token model if you prefer

Two things I want to confirm with you (and copied Ben/Marissa to weigh in):
1) Is the seat->credit mapping acceptable as a commercial construct for Acme?
2) Do you need a hard SLA on trace retrieval latency for long-tail queries (30/90 day buckets)? That changes our infra costs a bit.

I've attached the draft term sheet and a simple cost model. If it looks broadly right, I'll send a short redlineable term sheet with a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acme_PROPOSAL_observability_v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Elena Roberts <elena@acmedata.com>

Subject: Re: Structuring seat-linked observability credits and retention tiers

Jordan — thanks for the clear deck. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 
1) On seat-linked credits: can credits be applied retroactively if we add seats mid-quarter (our launches are bursty)?
2) For tracing SLA: our product team needs 99.95% read availability for traces up to 30 days; 90/120 day reads can be lower. Can you map the cost delta?
3) How would this interact with committed throughput on Dedicated (we'll likely want a small Dedicated pool for predictable latency)?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week.

—Elena

elena@acmedata.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Structuring seat-linked observability credits and retention tiers

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Elena's questions. See quoted below. My thoughts: allow retroactive application within the quarter but not across quarters (keeps forecasting sane), and offer 99.95% trace read SLA for 30 days as a paid upgrade (small premium) — but need pricing guidance on the premium and an estimate of infra/hour for warm vs cold trace storage. Also need to confirm how this ties into Dedicated throughput commitments.

Quoted: 
> On seat-linked credits: can credits be applied retroactively if we add seats mid-quarter (our launches are bursty)?
> For tracing SLA: our product team needs 99.95% read availability for traces up to 30 days; 90/120 day reads can be lower. Can you map the cost delta?
> How would this interact with committed throughput on Dedicated (we'll likely want a small Dedicated pool for predictable latency)?

Thanks — can you run a quick cost vs margin sketch and a recommended commercial position? I think Acme is likely to commit if we keep the overage predictable.

-Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Structuring seat-linked observability credits and retention tiers

Jordan / Marissa — quick pricing sketch and recommended approach: 

1) Retroactive credits: allow seat additions to be applied retroactively within the same billing quarter (max lookback 45 days) — we cap at the quarter to protect forecasting. Communicate this clearly in the MOU.

2) SLA tiers:
- Standard (14-day): no SLA — included
- Premium (30-day): 99.95% read SLA — surcharge of +12% on observability add-on ARR (covers hot storage + priority routing)
- Extended (90/120-day): 99.5% read SLA for 90-day bucket — surcharge +6% on the incremental retention above 30-day bucket (cold tier pricing)

3) Dedicated interaction: treat Dedicated throughput commitments separately. For small Dedicated pools we propose 1) a fixed egress/throughput buffer included in the Dedicated commitment and 2) observability credits applied at tenant level (not tied to GPU pool). If Acme wants the observability storage co-located, add a co-location premium (one-time) and a small monthly ops surcharge.

4) Overage handling: keep $/GB for overage but add a blended option: if they'd prefer predictable cost we can offer a capped overage at 125% of forecast for a 10% uplift on ARR.

Margin and next steps: this structure preserves ~40% gross margin on the observability add-on under conservative usage assumptions. Recommend offering a one-time onboarding credit (2 weeks of trace ingestion) in lieu of a price reduction — easier to account for.

If that's acceptable I'll draft a revised term sheet and updated XLS cost model for Jordan to send to Acme.

—Ben

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Roberts <elena@acmedata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Structuring seat-linked observability credits and retention tiers

Elena — thanks for the specifics. Based on internal alignment we've adjusted the commercial structure and attached a concise term sheet (revised_term_sheet_20260616.xlsx). Highlights: 
- We will apply seat-linked retention credits retroactively within the same quarter (up to 45 days lookback).
- Premium Tracing SLA (30-day) available at +12% observability ARR; 90-day cold reads priced at incremental +6% above the 30-day tier.
- Dedicated: observability credits apply tenant-wide; co-location/infrastructure preference will be charged as a one-time set-up fee.
- Overage cap option: 125% of forecast for a 10% uplift on ARR (optional).

If that matches what you need we'll generate a redlineable MOU and a DocuSign link. We can also convert the retention credit model into a blended token model if you'd prefer simpler per-call economics — let us know which you prefer.
